mainTopic: Burial of women, the death of צדיקים, signs in the timing of death, מזל, and stories of how חכמים died
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate about setting a woman's bier down in the street. The first view says the rule is only for a woman who died in childbirth, and רבי אלעזר says it is for all women, because מרים was buried right where she died. From that פסוק, רבי אלעזר also learns that מרים died בנשיקה like משה, and רבי אמי and רבי אלעזר teach that the death of צדיקים brings כפרה, like פרה אדומה and בגדי כהונה. A ברייתא then names kinds of death by how many days a person was sick, with five days being the normal death of all people, and by the age at death, from כרת at fifty up to גבורות at eighty. רב יוסף celebrates passing sixty, and זוגא דמהדייב explains that after eighty even a sudden death is a מיתת נשיקה. רבא teaches that life, children and sustenance depend on מזל, not merit, and proves it from רבה and רב חסדא. The amud ends with stories of how great חכמים died and how some of them held off the מלאך המות for a while: רבא, רב נחמן, רבי אלעזר, רב ששת, רב אשי, רב חסדא and רבי חייא.

steps.title: The rule applies only to a woman who died in childbirth
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion limits the rule against setting a woman's bier down in the street to a חיה, a woman who died in childbirth. Other women's biers may be set down.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught only about a woman who died in childbirth. But the biers of other women may be set down in the street.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a statement that began on the previous daf. It limits the ברייתא's rule about not setting down a woman's bier to a woman who died in childbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a woman's bier should not be put down in the street. This opinion narrows that rule to a חיה, who is still bleeding, so there is a special concern for her dignity. For any other woman, putting the bier down is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman giving birth; here, a woman who died in childbirth

phrases.english: [It was taught] only about a woman who died in childbirth.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous daf: 'they only taught this about...'

phrases.english: But other women — we may set [their biers] down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חָיָה. אֲבָל שְׁאָר נָשִׁים מַנִּיחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the limiting statement on the ברייתא begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the bier of a woman who died in childbirth may not be set down in the street. Other women's biers may be.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the rule applies to all women
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that no woman's bier should be set down in the street. He proves it from the פסוק about מרים, whose burial was close to her death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Even other women's biers are not set down, as it is written: 'And מרים died there and was buried there.' Burial is close to death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with the limit in step 1. He says the rule covers every woman, and brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word ״שם״ shows that מרים was buried in the very place she died, with no delay or long procession. From this, רבי אלעזר learns that any woman should be buried quickly and close to where she died, without stopping in the street.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Even other women [are not set down],
as it is written: 'And Miriam died there and was buried there' —
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:1

phrases.english: burial is close to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שְׁאָר הַנָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 1's limit and widens the rule to all women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No woman's bier is set down in the street, because a woman should be buried close to the place of her death.
steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק becomes the base for the next several teachings about מרים.

steps.title: מרים also died by a divine kiss
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds a second teaching from the same פסוק: מרים died בנשיקה, like משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: מרים too died by a kiss.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר now uses the same פסוק about מרים to teach something new, not about halacha but about how she died. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״אף״ (also) compares her to משה, whose death the Torah describes as ״על פי ה׳״. Dying בנשיקה is the gentlest kind of death, given to the most righteous people.

keyTerms.meaning: By a (divine) kiss, the gentlest kind of death

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Miriam too died by a kiss.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אַף מִרְיָם בִּנְשִׁיקָה מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 2 for a new, aggadic teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרים died בנשיקה, like משה.

steps.title: The source: a word link between מרים and משה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is a גזירה שוה: the word ״שם״ appears by מרים's death and by משה's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'there' and 'there' from משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for step 3. It links the word ״שם״ in מרים's פסוק to the same word in משה's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About משה the Torah says he died ״שם״ and ״על פי ה׳״, by the mouth of ה׳, which means a kiss. Because the same word ״שם״ is used by מרים, she shares that detail.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning from the same word used in two places

phrases.english: It is learned from 'there' [and] 'there' from Moshe.
phrases.notes: משה's פסוק is דברים 34:5: 'And משה died there... by the mouth of ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתְיָא ״שָׁם״ ״שָׁם״ מִמֹּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 3's claim.
steps.raayaSupportSource: גזירה שוה of ״שם״ between במדבר 20:1 and דברים 34:5

steps.title: Why doesn't the verse say it openly about מרים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah did not write ״על פי ה׳״ about מרים as it did about משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was 'by the mouth of ה׳' not said about her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a natural question about step 4. If מרים died the same way as משה, why doesn't the Torah say so openly? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Needing a גזירה שוה to learn this seems strange when the Torah could have used the same clear words. The question tests why the text is silent.

keyTerms.meaning: By the mouth of ה׳ (a divine kiss)

phrases.english: And for what reason was it not said about her
'by the mouth of ה׳'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 4's derivation was needed instead of an explicit פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah does not write ״על פי ה׳״ about מרים openly.

steps.title: It would be unseemly to say it
steps.stepSummary: The Torah does not say it openly because it would be unseemly to describe a woman dying by a divine kiss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the matter is unseemly to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 5. The Torah avoided writing it openly out of respect, so it is hinted only through the word link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact is true, but the Torah chose modest wording. So the meaning is passed on through the גזירה שוה rather than written in plain words.
steps.whatToRemember: מרים died בנשיקה like משה. It is learned from ״שם״/״שם״, and the Torah does not say it openly out of respect.

phrases.english: Because the matter is unseemly to say.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁגְּנַאי הַדָּבָר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Writing ״על פי ה׳״ openly about a woman would be unseemly, so the Torah only hints at it.

steps.title: מרים's death next to פרה אדומה: the death of צדיקים atones
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains that מרים's death is placed right after פרה אדומה to teach that, just as the פרה brings כפרה, the death of צדיקים brings כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Why was מרים's death placed next to the section of פרה אדומה? To tell you: just as פרה אדומה atones, so too the death of צדיקים atones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי asks and answers his own question about the order of the Torah's sections. Placing two sections next to each other teaches that they share something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרה אדומה brings כפרה. Because מרים's death comes right next to it, we learn that the death of צדיקים also brings כפרה for the people. The question is part of the teaching itself, not an attack on anything earlier.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Why was the death of Miriam placed next
to the section of the red heifer?
To tell you:
just as the red heifer atones —
so too the death of the righteous atones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה מִיתַת מִרְיָם לְפָרָשַׁת פָּרָה אֲדוּמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new aggadic teaching about מרים's death, based on where her פסוק is placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of צדיקים atones, like פרה אדומה.

steps.title: אהרן's death next to בגדי כהונה: the same lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a parallel teaching. אהרן's death is placed next to בגדי כהונה to teach that, just as they atone, the death of צדיקים atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Why was אהרן's death placed next to בגדי כהונה? Just as בגדי כהונה atone, so too the death of צדיקים atones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same style of teaching for אהרן. This adds a second source for the idea that the death of צדיקים brings כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בגדי כהונה bring כפרה. Because אהרן's death is placed next to them, his death, and the death of צדיקים in general, also atones. This repeats the lesson of step 7 from a different פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources teach the same idea: מרים next to פרה אדומה and אהרן next to בגדי כהונה. The death of צדיקים brings כפרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Why was the death of Aharon placed next
to the priestly garments?
Just as the priestly garments atone —
so too the death of the righteous atones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה מִיתַת אַהֲרֹן לְבִגְדֵי כְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 7 with a second source for the same lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of צדיקים atones, like בגדי כהונה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: sudden death and death after one day of sickness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא calls sudden death a 'snatched' death, and death after one day of sickness a 'rushed' death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone dies suddenly, that is a 'snatched' death. If he was sick for one day and then died, that is a 'rushed' death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא that gives names to different kinds of death. It begins with the two fastest kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is how long the person was sick before he died. No sickness at all is 'snatched' (מיתה חטופה). One day of sickness is 'rushed' (מיתה דחופה). The list will keep going, day by day, in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
A 'snatched' death, when a person is taken suddenly
A 'rushed' death, after only one day of sickness

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one died suddenly,
this is a 'snatched' death.
If he became sick for one day and died,
this is a 'rushed' death.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵת פִּתְאוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the teachings that the death of צדיקים brings כפרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sudden death is מיתה חטופה; death after one day of sickness is מיתה דחופה.

steps.title: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל: one day of sickness is a death by plague
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל calls death after one day of sickness מיתת מגפה, and proves it from יחזקאל's wife, who died within one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן גמליאל says: this one-day death is a 'death by plague.' The פסוק says: 'Son of man, I am taking from you the delight of your eyes by a plague.' And it says: 'I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different name to the death after one day of sickness. It brings two פסוקים from יחזקאל as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק calls the death of יחזקאל's wife a מגפה. The second פסוק shows she died between morning and evening, inside one day. Put together, a death after one day is called מיתת מגפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the name the ברייתא gave
Death by plague, a death that strikes quickly
The delight of your eyes; here it means יחזקאל's wife

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Gamliel says:
This is a death by plague,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the case just mentioned: sick for one day and then died.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"Son of man, behold, I am taking from you
the delight of your eyes by a plague,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 24:16

phrases.english: and it is written: "So I spoke to the people in the morning
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 24:18

phrases.english: and my wife died in the evening."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: זוֹ הִיא מִיתַת מַגֵּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another name for the one-day death described in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death after one day of sickness is called מיתת מגפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 24:16 and 24:18: his wife died 'by a plague,' from morning to evening.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: two to five days of sickness
steps.stepSummary: Two days is a 'pushed off' death, three is rebuke, four is reprimand, and five is the normal death of all people.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was sick two days and died, it is a 'pushed off' death. Three days is a death of rebuke. Four days is a death of reprimand. Five days is the normal death of all people.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with its list, day by day, up to five days of sickness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fewer the days, the harsher the death sounds: two, three, and four days still carry a message of rebuke. Only five days of sickness counts as ordinary, the way everyone dies. This number five is what the next step will try to source in a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'pushed off' death, after two days of sickness
Rebuke, after three days of sickness
Reprimand, after four days of sickness
The death of all people, the normal kind of death

steps.whatToRemember: Five days of sickness before death is the normal 'death of all people.' Fewer days carry a message of rebuke.

phrases.english: If he was sick two days and died,
this is a 'pushed off' death.
Three days: a death of rebuke.
Four days: a death of reprimand.

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה — זוֹ הִיא מִיתַת כׇּל אָדָם.
phrases.english: Five days: this is the death of all people.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי יָמִים וָמֵת — זוֹ הִיא מִיתָה דְּחוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list after רבי חנניא בן גמליאל's different name for the one-day death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two days is דחויה, three is גערה, four is נזיפה, and five is מיתת כל אדם.

steps.title: רבי חנין finds the number five in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין counts five in the words 'הן קרבו ימיך למות': הן is one, קרבו is two, ימיך is two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said: What is the פסוק for this? 'Behold, your days approach that you must die.' 'הן' means one, 'קרבו' (plural) means two, 'ימיך' (plural) means two. That makes five.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנין gives a source for the idea that five days of sickness is the normal death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the פסוק said to משה before his death. A plural word counts as at least two, so קרבו and ימיך give four together. Add one for הן, and you get five.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק? Where is the source?
Behold; here it is counted as 'one'

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanin said: What is the verse for this?
"Behold, your days approach that you must die."
phrases.notes: דברים 31:14

phrases.english: "Behold" is one,
"approach" is two,
phrases.notes: It is a plural word, and plural means at least two.

phrases.english: "your days" is two,
so that makes five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנִין, מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from a פסוק for the five days in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That five days of sickness is the normal death of all people.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 31:14, counting the words הן (1), קרבו (2), ימיך (2).

steps.title: Why הן counts as one
steps.stepSummary: The word הן counts as one because in Greek the word for 'one' is 'hen.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How is 'הן' one? Because in the Greek language they call the number one 'hen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the one part of רבי חנין's count that is not obvious: why the word הן means one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is easy to see why plural words count as two. But הן just means 'behold.' The גמרא answers that the Greek word for one sounds like הן, so it can count as one.
steps.confusionAlert: הן does not mean 'one' in Hebrew. It means 'behold.' The count of one comes only from the Greek word that sounds the same.

phrases.english: "Behold" is one?
Because in the Greek language
they call the number one "hen."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הֵן״ חַד, שֶׁכֵּן בְּלָשׁוֹן יְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains one word in רבי חנין's count from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word הן can mean the number one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In Greek, the word for one is 'hen.'

steps.title: What it means to die at fifty, fifty-two, or sixty
steps.stepSummary: Dying at fifty is כרת, at fifty-two is like שמואל הרמתי, and at sixty is מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one dies at fifty years old, that is death of כרת. At fifty-two, that is the death of שמואל הרמתי. At sixty, that is death at the hands of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from days of sickness to age, and lists what dying at certain ages means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the measure was how many days a person was sick. Now the measure is how old he was when he died. Fifty is linked to כרת, fifty-two is named as the age at which שמואל הרמתי died, and sixty is linked to death בידי שמים. רבה will explain this list in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off; a punishment from Heaven for very serious sins
שמואל the נביא, from the town of רמה
Death at the hands of Heaven, a punishment from Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives meaning to death in two ways: by how many days a person was sick, and by how old he was.

phrases.english: If one died at fifty years old,
this is death of karet.
At fifty-two years old,

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא מִיתָתוֹ שֶׁל שְׁמוּאֵל הָרָמָתִי.
phrases.english: this is the death of Samuel from Ramah.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשִּׁים — זוֹ הִיא מִיתָה בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: At sixty, this is death at the hands of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה — זוֹ הִיא מִיתַת כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from length of sickness to age at death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death at fifty is כרת, at fifty-two is like שמואל הרמתי, and at sixty is מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: A verse hinting that sixty is death by the hand of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a פסוק for the rule about sixty: the word בכלח adds up to sixty in גימטריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Where is the verse for this? It says, 'You shall come to the grave in ripe age (בכלח).' The word בכלח adds up to sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives a source for the last rule in step 14, that dying at sixty is מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number values of the letters in בכלח add up to sixty. So the פסוק about coming to the grave hints at the age of sixty. This backs up the rule with a hint from תנ״ך.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for the source)
In ripe age (a word from איוב)
Counting the number value of Hebrew letters

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: What is the verse?
phrases.notes: He means the source for dying at sixty being death by the hand of Heaven, from step 14.

phrases.english: As it is written: "You shall come to the grave in ripe age"
phrases.notes: איוב 5:26

phrases.english: "Bekhelach" in gematria adds up to sixty.
phrases.notes: ב is 2, כ is 20, ל is 30, ח is 8, so the total is 60.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי קרא דכתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק for the sixty-year rule in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Dying at sixty is מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 5:26, where the word בכלח has the number value of sixty.

steps.title: Seventy is old age and eighty is strength
steps.stepSummary: Dying at seventy is called שיבה (old age), and at eighty גבורות (strength), based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Seventy is old age. Eighty is strength, as it says: 'The days of our years are seventy years, and if with strength, eighty years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes on: seventy is a normal old age, and eighty is a sign of extra strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These ages are no longer signs of punishment. The פסוק in תהלים calls seventy the normal length of life and eighty a life of special strength.

phrases.english: Seventy is old age.
Eighty is strength,
as it is written: "The days of our years are seventy years,
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:10

phrases.english: and if with strength, eighty years."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes on with the list of ages from step 14, now covering seventy and eighty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death at seventy is שיבה, and death at eighty is גבורות.

steps.title: Every age from fifty to sixty counts as an early death
steps.stepSummary: רבה says any death between fifty and sixty is מיתת כרת. The list did not mention every year out of respect for שמואל הרמתי, who died at fifty-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: From fifty until sixty years is a death of כרת. The reason the list did not count all those years is the honor of שמואל הרמתי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה widens the כרת rule from step 14 to cover the whole range from fifty to sixty. He also explains why the list did not spell that out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 named only fifty, fifty-two, and sixty. רבה says all the years in between are really כרת too. The list avoided saying so openly because שמואל died at fifty-two, and it did not want to call his death a כרת death.

keyTerms.meaning: A death that shows a punishment of being cut off early
That it did not count them

steps.confusionAlert: רבה does not say שמואל's death was a punishment. He says the list did not group fifty-two with כרת to protect שמואל's honor.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
From fifty until sixty years:
this is a death of karet.
And the reason it did not count them all
is because of the honor of Shmuel from Ramah.
phrases.notes: He died at fifty-two, as we saw in step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens and explains the fifty-to-sixty part of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All deaths from fifty to sixty are מיתת כרת. The list skipped the years in between out of respect for שמואל.

steps.title: רב יוסף celebrates turning sixty
steps.stepSummary: When רב יוסף turned sixty, he made a celebration for the חכמים, saying he had now passed the age of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יוסף turned sixty, he made a festive day for the Rabbis. He said: I have gotten out of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story putting רבה's rule into practice. It sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since dying before sixty counts as כרת, reaching sixty meant רב יוסף was safe from that sign. He thanked ה׳ by celebrating with the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף כִּי הֲוָה בַּר שִׁיתִּין,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, when he turned sixty,
made a festive day for the Rabbis.
He said: I have gotten out of karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב יוסף כי הוה בר שיתין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that uses רבה's fifty-to-sixty rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reaching sixty means one has passed the age of כרת.

steps.title: אביי: you still have not escaped the 'כרת of days'
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: you passed the כרת of years, but you can still die in a way that counts as כרת by the number of days of sickness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Even if you, master, got out of the כרת of years, did you get out of the כרת of days?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of signs: the age a person dies, and how fast the death comes (steps 9-11). Passing sixty only removes the first kind, so אביי asks why רב יוסף is celebrating so fully.

keyTerms.meaning: The כרת of days (dying very quickly)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דִּנְפַק לֵיהּ מָר מִכָּרֵת דִּשְׁנֵי,
phrases.english: Granted that master got out of the karet of years,
did master get out of the karet of days?
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the earlier list about dying after only a few days of sickness.

steps.triggerLanguage: נהי דנפק ליה מר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reason for celebrating.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that he is free of כרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Passing sixty only removes the age sign. A sudden or quick death could still be a sign of punishment.

steps.title: Hold on to at least half
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that he has at least escaped one of the two kinds of כרת, and that is worth celebrating.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: At least hold half in your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees the danger of the 'days' kind is still there. But getting past one of the two signs is already a real reason to be happy.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Hold at least half in your hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: נקוט לך מיהא פלגא בידך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement: he admits the point but holds that partial safety is still worth celebrating.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the celebration made no sense while one danger remained.
steps.terutzMaskana: Escaping one of the two kinds of כרת is already a real gain.

steps.title: רב הונא dies suddenly and the חכמים are worried
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא died suddenly, and the חכמים worried it might be a bad sign about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא died suddenly, and the Rabbis were worried.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story sets up a worry. Does a sudden death show that something was wrong? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on the earlier lists, a sudden death looks like a sign of punishment. So the חכמים were troubled about a great person like רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (his soul came to rest)

phrases.english: Rav Huna passed away suddenly,
and the Rabbis were worried.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב הונא נח נפשיה פתאום
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that tests the rule about sudden death.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רב הונא's sudden death a sign of punishment?

steps.title: After eighty, a sudden death is a 'death by a kiss'
steps.stepSummary: זוגא דמהדייב teaches that the bad signs apply only before eighty. Someone past eighty who dies suddenly has a מיתת נשיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: זוגא דמהדייב taught them: They only said this about someone who did not reach the age of strength. But if he reached the age of strength, it is death by a kiss.
steps.whatsHappening: זוגא דמהדייב answers the worry and calms the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs about sudden death apply only to someone under eighty (גבורות). After eighty, a quick death is not a punishment at all. It is a gentle, loving death, called a 'kiss.'

keyTerms.meaning: Death by a kiss, a gentle death from ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: Under sixty, the age of death can be a sign of כרת. At seventy it is שיבה and at eighty גבורות. After eighty, even a sudden death is a gentle מיתת נשיקה.

phrases.english: Zuga from Hadayeiv taught them:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לִגְבוּרוֹת,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he had not reached the age of strength,
phrases.notes: The age of strength is eighty, from step 16.

phrases.english: but if he reached the age of strength,
this is death by a kiss.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא שנו אלא שלא הגיע לגבורות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sudden-death signs apply only before eighty. After eighty, a sudden death is a מיתת נשיקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a limit on the whole list of bad signs. Past eighty, a quick death is seen as a kindness, not a punishment.

steps.title: Life, children, and sustenance depend on מזל
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that how long you live, whether you have children, and how much income you have are not decided by your merit but by מזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Life, children, and food are not dependent on merit. They are dependent on מזל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new general rule. Three areas of life are not handed out according to how good a person is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps discussed age and the meaning of an early or sudden death. רבא adds a key idea: a short life, or a lack of children or money, does not automatically mean a person lacked זכות. These three things follow a different system, called מזל.

keyTerms.meaning: Life, meaning the length of one's life
Merit earned by one's good deeds
מזל: what is assigned to a person from Heaven, not earned

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying good deeds don't matter. רבא is only saying that these three specific things are not handed out as a direct reward for merit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the previous discussion of early death cannot simply be read as a judgment on a person's righteousness.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Life, children, and sustenance,
the matter does not depend on merit,
rather, the matter depends on mazal.
phrases.notes: Think of מזל here as what Heaven has set for a person ahead of time, as opposed to what he earns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: חַיֵּי, בְּנֵי וּמְזוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of length of life and the meaning of how a person dies, adding a general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Length of life, children, and sustenance depend on מזל, not on merit.

steps.title: רבה and רב חסדא were equally righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins his proof. רבה and רב חסדא were both צדיקים, and both could bring rain when they prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבה and רב חסדא were both righteous חכמים. One would pray and rain would come, and the other would pray and rain would come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up his proof. First he shows that the two חכמים had equal merit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting rain through prayer is a sign of great זכות. By showing that both men had this power, רבא shows that merit cannot explain any difference between them. That sets up the contrast in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: "Master"; here, one חכם and then the other

phrases.english: For behold, Rabba and Rav Chisda
were both righteous Sages;
this master would pray and rain would come,
phrases.notes: The first מר is one of the two חכמים, and the second מר is the other one.

phrases.english: and that master would pray and rain would come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא רַבָּה וְרַב חִסְדָּא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ רַבָּנַן צַדִּיקֵי הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רבא's statement by establishing that the two חכמים had equal merit.
steps.raayaObject: That life, children, and sustenance depend on מזל and not on merit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The example of רבה and רב חסדא, who were equal in righteousness.

steps.title: Their lives and families were completely different
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא lived to 92, but רבה lived only to 40. רב חסדא's house had sixty weddings, while רבה's house had sixty tragedies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא lived ninety-two years, while רבה lived forty. רב חסדא's household had sixty wedding celebrations, while רבה's household had sixty bereavements.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows the contrast in the first two of his three areas: length of life (חיי) and children (בני).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their merit was equal, yet one lived more than twice as long as the other. One family was blessed with many children and weddings, while the other suffered many deaths. Merit cannot explain the gap, so it must be מזל.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא חֲיָה תִּשְׁעִין וְתַרְתֵּין שְׁנִין,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda lived ninety-two years;
Rabba lived forty.
The house of Rav Chisda had sixty wedding feasts;
the house of Rabba had sixty bereavements.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא חֲיָה תִּשְׁעִין וְתַרְתֵּין שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the contrast in life and children between the two equally righteous חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: That life and children depend on מזל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The different lifespans and family fortunes of רב חסדא and רבה.

steps.title: Their food and income were completely different
steps.stepSummary: In רב חסדא's house even the dogs got fine flour bread, more than they wanted. In רבה's house even the people lacked plain barley bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רב חסדא's house there was fine flour bread for the dogs, and nobody wanted it. In רבה's house there was barley bread for people, and even that could not be found.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof with the third area, sustenance (מזוני).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now all three items in רבא's statement are shown. With equal merit, one man had so much food that even the dogs had plenty, and the other man's household was short on the cheapest bread. So income, like life and children, depends on מזל.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour, here bread made from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבה and רב חסדא were equal in זכות but completely different in life, children, and sustenance. That is רבא's proof that these three depend on מזל.

phrases.english: In the house of Rav Chisda, fine-flour bread for the dogs
and it was not wanted;
in the house of Rabba, barley bread for people
and it was not found.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא סְמִידָא לְכַלְבֵי וְלָא מִתְבְּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof with the third item, sustenance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between the abundance in רב חסדא's house and the poverty in רבה's house.

steps.title: רבא's three requests from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבא asked Heaven for three things: the wisdom of רב הונא, the wealth of רב חסדא, and the humility of רבה בר רב הונא. He received the first two but not the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: I asked Heaven for three things. They gave me two and did not give me one. The wisdom of רב הונא and the wealth of רב חסדא, they gave me. The humility of רבה בר רב הונא, they did not give me.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב חסדא's wealth was just mentioned, the גמרא brings another statement of רבא. In it, רבא tells which personal gifts he prayed for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a related story, not part of the proof. רבא lists three admired qualities from three different חכמים. He reports that his prayers for wisdom and wealth were answered, but his prayer for that great level of humility was not.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה בר רב הונא is a different person from the רבה in the earlier steps who lived only forty years.

phrases.english: And Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי תְּלָת מִילֵּי בְּעַאי קַמֵּי שְׁמַיָּא,
phrases.english: These three things I requested before Heaven;
two they gave me,
one they did not give me:
the wisdom of Rav Huna
and the wealth of Rav Chisda,
and they gave them to me.
The humility of Rabba bar Rav Huna
they did not give me.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי תְּלָת מִילֵּי בְּעַאי קַמֵּי שְׁמַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought because the previous step mentioned רב חסדא's wealth; another statement by the same speaker, רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא received the wisdom of רב הונא and the wealth of רב חסדא, but not the humility of רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.title: רבא asks his brother to ask the מלאך המות to be gentle
steps.stepSummary: As רבא is dying, he asks his brother רב שעורים to tell the מלאך המות not to cause him pain. He explains that once his מזל has been handed over, the מלאך המות no longer pays attention to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שעורים, רבא's brother, was sitting before רבא and saw that he was slipping toward death. רבא said to him: Please tell him (the מלאך המות) not to cause me pain. רב שעורים said: Aren't you his friend? רבא answered: Once my מזל has been handed over, he pays no attention to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about the death of רבא. רבא asks his brother to ask the מלאך המות to be gentle with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שעורים assumes that a צדיק like רבא is close with the מלאך המות and can ask for anything. רבא answers that once the time of death has been decided, even that closeness does not help. This ties back to רבא's earlier teaching that length of life depends on מזל, not merit.

keyTerms.meaning: Dozing; here it means slipping into death
To cause me pain or suffering
His close friend (literally, his wedding companion)
The מזל (fate) has been handed over, meaning death has been decreed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows רבא living out his own rule from step 23: even a great צדיק cannot change his time once his מזל is set.

phrases.english: Rav Seorim, Rava's brother,
was sitting before Rava.
He saw that he was dozing.
phrases.notes: "Dozing" here means רבא was drifting toward death.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: Let the master tell him
not to cause me pain.
phrases.notes: "Him" is the מלאך המות. The גמרא doesn't name him but assumes you know.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָר לָאו שׁוֹשְׁבִינֵיהּ הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Isn't the master his friend?
He said to him: Since the fate has been handed over,
he pays no attention to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׂעוֹרִים אֲחוּהּ דְּרָבָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבא's teachings about מזל to a story about רבא's own death, which shows the same idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a person's מזל for death is handed over, even a friendship with the מלאך המות does not help.

steps.title: רבא appears after death and describes the pain
steps.stepSummary: רב שעורים asks רבא to appear to him after death. רבא appears and says the pain of death was like the small prick of a bloodletting knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שעורים said: Please appear to me after you die. רבא appeared to him. He asked: Did you feel pain? רבא said: Like the prick of a bloodletting knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues after רבא's death. רבא appears in a dream and tells his brother what dying felt like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבא could not get the מלאך המות's special attention, his death was only mildly painful. A quick, small prick is the picture of a short and light pain.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him appear to me (in a dream, after death)
The prick of a bloodletting knife

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master appear to me.
phrases.notes: He means: show yourself to me in a dream after you die.

phrases.english: He appeared to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמָר צַעֲרָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did the master have pain?
He said to him: Like the prick of a bloodletting knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִיתְחֲזֵי לִי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of רבא's death by describing what it felt like.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's death was only as painful as a small bloodletting prick.

steps.title: רב נחמן says no one is important in Heaven
steps.stepSummary: A similar story: רב נחמן is dying and asks רבא to tell the מלאך המות not to cause him pain. When רבא says he is an important person, רב נחמן answers that in Heaven no one counts as important.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא was sitting before רב נחמן and saw him slipping toward death. רב נחמן said: Please tell him (the מלאך המות) not to cause me pain. רבא said: Aren't you an important person? רב נחמן answered: Who is important, who is honored, who is perfect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, parallel story. This time רבא is at the deathbed of his teacher רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thinks רב נחמן's high status should protect him from a painful death. רב נחמן says that before Heaven, human greatness counts for nothing. The repeated wording invites us to compare this story with רבא's own.
steps.confusionAlert: In this story the roles are switched. Now רבא is the visitor, and רב נחמן is the one who is dying.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: Rava was sitting before Rav Nachman.
He saw that he was dozing.
He (Rav Nachman) said to him: Let the master tell him
not to cause me pain.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָר לָאו אָדָם חָשׁוּב הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Isn't the master an important person?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן חֲשִׁיב, מַאן סְפִין, מַאן רְקִיעַ!
phrases.english: He said to him: Who is important? Who is honored? Who is complete?
phrases.notes: He means that up in Heaven, nobody can count on being important.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel deathbed story with almost the same wording as רבא's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Heaven, no human can count on his own importance.

steps.title: רב נחמן describes a gentle death but great fear
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן appears to רבא after death and says dying was as gentle as pulling a hair out of milk. Still, he would not want to come back to this world, because the fear was so great.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Please appear to me. He appeared to him. רבא asked: Did you feel pain? He said: Like pulling a hair out of milk. But if הקדוש ברוך הוא told me to go back to that world as I was, I would not want to, because the fear of it is so great.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן appears in a dream and describes his death. The pain was tiny, but the fear was huge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling a hair from milk is smooth and effortless, which is gentler than רבא's "prick." Even so, רב נחמן adds something new: the terror of dying is so great that he would refuse to live again if it meant facing death a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: Like pulling a hair out of milk; something very easy and gentle
"That world"; here it means this physical world
Its fear, the terror of it

steps.whatToRemember: For these צדיקים, the pain of death was small, but the fear of the experience was overwhelming.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master appear to me.
He appeared to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמָר צַעֲרָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did the master have pain?
He said to him: Like pulling a hair out of milk.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמַר לִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: And if the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to me,
"Go to that world as you were,"
phrases.notes: Speaking from Heaven, he calls our physical world "that world."

phrases.english: I would not want it, because its fear is great.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּמִישְׁחַל בִּנִיתָא מֵחֲלָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב נחמן's story the same way רבא's story ended, and adds the point about fear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death was physically gentle for רב נחמן, but the fear was so great he would not want to go through it again.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר delays death while eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות appears to רבי אלעזר while he is eating תרומה. He argues that תרומה is called holy, so this is not the right moment. The moment passes and he lives on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר was eating תרומה. The מלאך המות appeared to him. He said: I am eating תרומה. Isn't it called holy? The moment passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about a צדיק who pushed off the מלאך המות. He did this by pointing to the holy food he was eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר argues that dying while eating something called קודש would be wrong. The מלאך המות accepts this, and the decreed moment passes. This shows that a מצוה being done can protect a person, at least for the moment.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, which is holy

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read step 28 as saying the time of death can never move. There רבא only said the מלאך המות would not listen to his request about pain once his מזל was handed over. Here רבי אלעזר points to the holiness of תרומה, and the moment passes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar was eating terumah.
He appeared to him. He said to him:
phrases.notes: The one who appeared is the מלאך המות, even though the גמרא doesn't name him.

phrases.english: I am eating terumah.
Isn't it called holy?
The moment passed for him.
phrases.notes: The time set for his death went by, and he kept living.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הֲוָה קָאָכֵיל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about a צדיק and the מלאך המות. This time the צדיק succeeds in delaying his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because רבי אלעזר was eating holy תרומה, the moment of his death passed.

steps.title: רב ששת refuses to die in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות appears to רב ששת in the marketplace. רב ששת tells him that dying in the street is like an animal's death, so he should come to his house instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מלאך המות appeared to רב ששת in the marketplace. רב ששת said to him: In the market, like an animal? Come to my house.
steps.whatsHappening: Another story in the series: רב ששת refuses to die in a public, undignified place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אלעזר in the previous step, רב ששת argues that this is not the right place or time. His point is human dignity: a person should die at home, not in the street like an animal.

phrases.english: The Angel of Death appeared to Rav Sheshet in the marketplace,
He said to him: In the market, like an animal?
Come to the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אִיתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ בְּשׁוּקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story: a sage pushes back on the timing or place of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sage asked not to die in an undignified public place.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for thirty days to review his learning
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות appears to רב אשי. רב אשי asks for thirty days to review his learning, because in Heaven they say: fortunate is the one who arrives with his learning in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מלאך המות appeared to רב אשי in the marketplace. He said to him: Give me thirty days so I can review my learning, for you people say: Fortunate is the one who comes here with his learning in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks for a short delay so he can review everything he learned before he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי uses Heaven's own saying as his argument. Since Heaven praises arriving with one's learning ready, the מלאך המות should give him time to prepare.

keyTerms.meaning: So I can review my learning
With his learning in his hand (fully remembered)

phrases.english: The Angel of Death appeared to Rav Ashi (in the marketplace),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיתְּרַח לִי תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין,
phrases.english: He said to him: Give me thirty days,
so that I may review my learning,
for you say:
phrases.notes: "You" means the ones up in Heaven.

phrases.english: Fortunate is the one who comes here
with his learning in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another sage asks for a delay, this time to review his learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arriving in Heaven with one's learning fully remembered is highly praised.

steps.title: On the thirtieth day: one leader's reign cannot overlap the next
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות returns on the thirtieth day. When רב אשי asks why he is in such a hurry, he answers that בר נתן's time to lead is pressing, and one reign cannot overlap another even by a hairbreadth.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the thirtieth day he came. רב אשי said to him: Why all this hurry? He answered: The foot of bar Natan is pushing, and one reign does not touch the next even by a hair's breadth.
steps.whatsHappening: The delay ends, and the מלאך המות explains why רב אשי cannot get more time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every leader has a fixed time. Once that time ends, the next leader (בר נתן) must begin right away, so רב אשי cannot stay even a moment longer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is all this? (Why the hurry?)
His foot is pushing (his turn is pressing)

steps.whatToRemember: Each leader's time is set exactly. One leader's time cannot cut into the next leader's time, even slightly.

phrases.english: On the thirtieth day he came.
He said to him: What is all this?
phrases.notes: רב אשי is asking why he can't be pushed off any longer.

phrases.english: The foot of bar Natan is pushing,
phrases.notes: בר נתן was ready to take over as the next leader.

phrases.english: and one reign does not touch its fellow
even by a hair's breadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיוֹם תְּלָתִין אֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רב אשי story: the delay ends and the reason no further delay is possible is given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One leader's time cannot overlap the next leader's time at all.

steps.title: רב חסדא's nonstop learning protects him
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות could not take רב חסדא because he never stopped learning. He sat on the cedar beam of the בית המדרש, the beam cracked, רב חסדא paused for a moment, and the מלאך המות took him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מלאך המות could not overcome רב חסדא, because his mouth was never silent from learning. He went up and sat on the cedar beam of the בית המדרש. The cedar cracked, רב חסדא fell silent, and the מלאך המות overcame him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story: as long as רב חסדא was learning, death could not touch him. A trick made him stop for a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning תורה works as protection from death. The מלאך המות had to create a distraction, the cracking beam, to break that protection for just one moment.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא הֲוָה יָכֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda, the Angel of Death could not overcome him,
because his mouth was never silent from learning,
so he went up and sat on the cedar of the study hall.
The cedar cracked, and Rav Chisda fell silent,
and the Angel of Death overcame him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא הֲוָה יָכֵיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another death story; here the sage's learning keeps death away until a trick interrupts it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Constant learning of תורה protected רב חסדא from death.

steps.title: The מלאך המות comes to רבי חייא disguised as a poor man
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות could not get near רבי חייא. One day he disguised himself as a poor man, knocked on the door and asked for bread, and רבי חייא's household brought it out to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מלאך המות could not come near רבי חייא. One day he disguised himself as a poor man, came and knocked on the door, and said: Bring me out bread. They brought it out to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The last story opens. The מלאך המות sets a trap by pretending to be a poor man, which sets up his argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא was so righteous that death could not approach him. By testing his kindness to the poor first, the מלאך המות prepares an argument that will turn that kindness toward himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Made himself look like, disguised himself

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא לָא הֲוָה מָצֵי לְמִיקְרַבא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: The Angel of Death was not able to come near Rabbi Chiyya,
One day he appeared to him as a poor man,
came, and knocked on the door,
He said to him: Bring out bread for me,
They brought it out for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא לָא הֲוָה מָצֵי לְמִיקְרַבא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like רב חסדא, רבי חייא is protected and the מלאך המות needs a trick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא's righteousness kept the מלאך המות from approaching him.

steps.title: Show mercy to me too: רבי חייא gives himself over
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המות argues: you have mercy on a poor man, so why not on me? He reveals who he is, shows a fiery rod, and רבי חייא gives himself over to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Master, don't you have mercy on a poor man? Then why don't you have mercy on 'that man' (me)? He revealed himself to him and showed him a rod of fire, and רבי חייא gave himself over to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The trap closes. The מלאך המות uses רבי חייא's own kindness as an argument, and רבי חייא accepts death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא had just shown mercy by giving what was asked. The מלאך המות says he should be just as merciful to him and let him do his job. The fiery rod proves who he is, and רבי חייא gives in willingly.

keyTerms.meaning: That man (a polite way of saying 'me')
He gave his soul over to him

steps.whatToRemember: In several of these stories, a sage's merit (learning, dignity, kindness) holds death back. רבי אלעזר's moment simply passes, but רב אשי, רב חסדא and רבי חייא are still taken when their time comes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלָאו קָא מְרַחֵם מָר אַעַנְיָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the master have mercy on a poor man?

phrases.aramaic: אַהָהוּא גַּבְרָא אַמַּאי לָא קָא מְרַחֵם מָר?
phrases.english: Why doesn't the master have mercy on that man?
phrases.notes: "That man" is the מלאך המות talking about himself.

phrases.english: He revealed himself to him,
showed him a rod of fire,
and Rabbi Chiyya gave himself over to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלָאו קָא מְרַחֵם מָר אַעַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the trap set up in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא accepted death willingly once the argument from mercy was made to him.
